what: Mapped water sources for the water-bodies stage (topobathy/water.py) and the flat-lake detector (axes.class_raster flat_lakes 'mapped'). A mapped polygon is an observation of its own kind -- where water was seen, by whom, when -- with no level; it never overrides a survey, it adds recall (small ponds under the detector's minimum, lakes the detector misses) and a check on both kinds of error (water.json: mapped_missed / bodies_unmapped).

sources.edge_note: the shoreline is trusted (fill._mapped_lake_sides, 2026-10-23): inside a lake polygon, raised land more than mapped_edge_dz_m above the water is floating or ice-cored unless an island polygon touches it; outside, within mapped_edge_near_m, it is shore or glacier. Add an island polygon to keep a real island; move the shoreline to move the glacier face.
sources.basis: hand-mapped for the KBSP map (Hig Lakes UTM5.shp, 3144 polygons: 1641 lakes, 1403 islands, 74 rivers); converted 2026-10-15 with ogr2ogr to EPSG:4326

sources.edge_note: WATER_REVIEW_PLAN.md W3: the reviewed water polygons. Start from a run's out/polygons_auto.geojson in QGIS, redraw what is wrong, set kind (lake | river | sea | island) and optionally level_m (a lake's one level), and set status to 'reviewed' -- only reviewed features are read. A reviewed polygon replaces the hig_lakes polygons at least half under it.

WATER_REVIEW_PLAN.md section 3: a run's out/water_flags.geojson with the reviewer's `disposition` filled in, saved here. island = the observation stands (an island inside the water); noise = the observation is void inside the water (open space for the interpolation; shore.py). polygon_edit / defer / blank: nothing (the suggestion stands).
